§95, p. 128: the causeway from the Granite Temple "straight up to the entrance of the temple of that Pyramid" is "a grand work, about 15 feet wide and over quarter of a mile long". Petrie writes "about", so the sigma is a foot and a half.

§95, p. 128: "over quarter of a mile long", a quarter of a mile being 1320 ft. A lower bound and not a length, so nothing is built from it; the causeway drawn between the two temples is checked against it.

How far the basalt platform is drawn proud of the ground. Petrie says in §28 that the pavement is "within two inches of the same level as" the limestone pavement round the Pyramid, and gives no thickness for the basalt; half a metre is chosen so the platform reads as the floor of a destroyed temple rather than vanishing into the ground it is flush with.

How deep the causeway is drawn. Petrie describes the rock "uniformly cut down to a sloping bed, on which has been laid apparently two layers of fine white limestone", all since torn up, and gives no depth; a metre draws the bed as a raised way along its ridge.
